newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump at close, hit by Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump at close, hit by Greenspan.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed sharply lower Wednesday after comments made by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan sent U.S. markets reeling.
Greenspan warned Wednesday that U.S. stock prices may have risen too far and hinted that the central bank may need to increase interest rates in the coming months.
"Greenspan's comments really scared the market, which had gained strongly and was ripe for profit-taking," a floor trader in Mexico City said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 48.54 points, or 1.23 percent, at 3,890.15. Trading volume was brisk at 112.5 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed off 55.03 points at 6,983.18 points.

American Depository Receipts in Telmex fell $1.50 to $39.125 on Wall Street, while its heavily weighted L shares dropped 32 centavos (4 cents) to 15.42 pesos ($1.98) in Mexico. The stock accounted for 24 percent of all shares traded during the session.
Analysts noted that Wednesday's fall came on the heels of three record closes in a row and said they were not overly concerned.
"We have many reasons for saying the bourse is still a good investment option," said Roberto Garcia, a fund manager at the Vector brokerage in Monterrey.
"Positive macroeconomic and microeconomic signals are luring foreign investors and many stocks are undervalued and still have upside potential to bolster the market," he added.
Technical analysts, meanwhile, said the market was taking a breather in order to consolidate recent sharp gains.
On the broad market, of a total of 122 stocks traded, decliners outweighed gainers by 77 to 19.
In percentage terms, soft-drinks bottler Gemex headed the pack with its B shares up 20 centavos (3 cents) at 3.50 pesos (45 cents).
Another notable gainer was steelmaker Hylsamex, whose B shares gained 1.20 pesos (15 cents) to 35.00 pesos ($4.48).
Financial group Serfin B shares ended off 14 centavos (2 cents) at 3.26 pesos (42 cents), while Abaco financial group's B shares fell 8 centavos (1 cent) to 1.42 pesos (18 cents).
Media group Televisa CPO shares ended off 4.90 pesos (63 cents) at 101.00 pesos ($12.94), on the back of its American Depository Receipts, which fell $1.50 to $25.875.
